raw_case_text:
A 12-year-old boy was admitted with complaints of mild abdominal pain and fever for one month. The intermittent and low-grade fever was relieved with analgesics. The mild and dull aching abdominal pain was confined to the right hypochondrium without any radiation. He also complained of a right upper abdominal bulge. There was a history of decreased appetite and weight loss of about 2-3 kg. The patient was haemodynamically stable. On abdominal examination, a firm and mildly tender mass was palpable 10 cm below the right costal margin, and the mass was not separately palpable from the liver. No prior history of hydatid disease, malignancy or any other comorbidity was found.
At USG, a large well-defined mass was found in the right lobe of the liver. It was solid and iso to hyperechoic in appearance with a few cystic areas (Figure 1a). No apparent internal vascularity was demonstrated on the colour Doppler study (Figure 1b). Based on the fever and USG findings, the possibility of an organised liver abscess or complicated hydatid cyst was considered. Empiric IV antibiotics and albendazole therapy were initiated. Liver function tests (liver enzymes, serum bilirubin and albumin levels) and complete haemogram were within the normal limits except for a low haemoglobin of 9 gm/dL. Total leucocyte counts and eosinophil counts were normal. Both hydatid (immunoglobulin G [IgG] titre-0.7; normal < 0.9) serology and amoebic serology (IgG titre-0.51; normal < 0.9) were non-reactive. Tumour markers were also within the normal limits. Serum alfa-fetoprotein (AFP), beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (beta-hCG) and carbohydrate antigen (CA-19-9) were 3.2 ng/mL (0-8.5), 0.8 IU/L (< 1.4) and 14 IU/mL (< 35), respectively.
Following failure to respond to antibiotic therapy, contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) and CE-MRI were requested for further evaluation of the lesion. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated a cystic appearing mass (attenuation: 20-25 HU) with peripheral internal vascularity (Figure 2a and b). MRI revealed T2 hyperintensity with heterogeneous internal content and fluid-fluid levels (Figure 3a and b). Areas of variable T1 hyperintensity were also seen, possibly due to haemorrhagic components of varying ages (Figure 3c). No enhancing solid tissue was seen within the lesion on post-contrast (gadopentetate dimeglumine) T1 weighted (T1W) images except for a few peripheral enhancing vessels as seen on CECT (Figure 3d). Diffusion-weighted images (DWI) revealed variable signal with foci of restricted diffusion (Figure 4a and b), corresponding to the haemorrhagic and necrotic areas.
A core needle biopsy was performed under USG guidance, using an 18G semi-automatic gun; however, the pathology was inconclusive because of the predominant necrotic material obtained during the biopsy procedure. Microbiological analysis of the biopsy sample was negative for bacteria, fungi, Entamoeba and parasites. Due to the non-resolving condition and inconclusive diagnosis, the patient finally underwent a right hepatectomy with removal of the lesion approximately 16 days after hospitalisation. The resected specimen revealed a large soft and friable tumour. The cut surface of the specimen revealed components of haemorrhage, necrosis and gelatinous material. There were no intra-operative or postoperative complications, and the patient was discharged on the 11th postoperative day in a stable condition.
Histopathological analysis of the resected specimen indicated that the tumour was composed of sheets of spindle cells with cellular pleomorphism, indistinct cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei. Immunohistochemistry showed CD10 membrane positivity, vimentin reactivity in spindle cells and negativity for Myo D1. These findings were suggestive of UES.
Postoperatively, the patient received six cycles of chemotherapy (vincristine + cyclophosphamide + epirubicin). He was asymptomatic with no recurrence on the last follow-up at 11 months after surgery.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 12-year-old boy presented with a 1-month history of mild right hypochondriac pain, intermittent low-grade fever, a right upper abdominal bulge, anorexia, and a 2-3 kg weight loss.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The child experienced dull, non-radiating right hypochondriac pain, analgesic-responsive intermittent low-grade fever, a visible right upper quadrant bulge, decreased appetite, and a 2-3 kg weight loss over 1 month. Empiric IV antibiotics and oral albendazole initiated after admission ultrasound failed to produce clinical improvement.
subjective.past_medical_history: No prior history of hydatid disease, malignancy, or other medical comorbidities.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for mild right hypochondriac pain, low-grade fever, right upper abdominal bulge, anorexia, and 2-3 kg weight loss.

objective.physical_examination: Hemodynamically stable; abdominal examination revealed a firm, mildly tender mass palpable 10 cm below the right costal margin and continuous with the liver.
objective.routine_investigations: Labs showed anemia (hemoglobin 9 g/dL) with normal WBC, eosinophil count, and liver function tests. Serum tumor markers were normal: AFP 3.2 ng/mL (0-8.5), beta-hCG 0.8 IU/L (<1.4), and CA 19-9 14 IU/mL (<35). Serologies for Echinococcus IgG (titer 0.7; normal <0.9) and Entamoeba histolytica IgG (titer 0.51; normal <0.9) were both non-reactive. Abdominal ultrasound with color Doppler showed a large well-defined iso-to-hyperechoic solid-cystic mass in the right hepatic lobe without internal Doppler flow.
objective.advanced_workup: Contrast-enhanced CT showed a cystic-appearing right hepatic mass (20-25 HU) with peripheral internal vessels; contrast-enhanced MRI demonstrated a T2-hyperintense mass with fluid-fluid levels, hemorrhagic T1-hyperintense foci, peripheral enhancing vessels, and restricted diffusion on DWI. After an 18G ultrasound-guided core biopsy yielded only sterile necrotic debris, right hepatectomy on hospital day 16 excised a large friable hemorrhagic/necrotic/gelatinous tumor; histopathology and IHC revealed pleomorphic spindle cell sheets positive for CD10 and vimentin and negative for MyoD1.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma (UES) of the right hepatic lobe initially mimicking an organized liver abscess or complicated hepatic hydatid cyst, confirmed by right hepatectomy histopathology and CD10/vimentin immunohistochemical positivity alongside negative hydatid and amebic serologies. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 11, completed 6 cycles of adjuvant vincristine, cyclophosphamide, and epirubicin chemotherapy, and remained recurrence-free at 11-month follow-up.
